title: Ordinary etale adjoint on strict coefficient systems
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and write $A_n=O/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type schemes over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; $Y$ need not be separated over $k$. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For a scheme $T$, use the category $\mathsf S_A(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ of strict varying-coefficient systems and its derived category defined in [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. On this category $j_{!,A}$ means termwise extension by zero and $p_{A,*}$ means termwise ordinary etale direct image, and put $F_{f,A}=Rp_{A,*}j_{!,A}$.

The functor $F_{f,A}:D(\mathsf S_A(X_{\mathrm{et}}))\to D(\mathsf S_A(Y_{\mathrm{et}}))$ has an $O$-linear exact right adjoint $G_{f,A}$ on these unbounded derived categories of systems. For every $n$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$e_nG_{f,A}M\cong f_n^\times(e_nM),$$
where $f_n^\times$ is the ordinary etale right adjoint at $A_n$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The comparisons identify the evaluated units, counits and transition maps with their adjunction mates at the finite coefficient levels. There is an integer $c_f\geq0$, independent of $n$, such that $G_{f,A}$ sends $D^{\geq a}(\mathsf S_A(Y_{\mathrm{et}}))$ into $D^{\geq a-c_f}(\mathsf S_A(X_{\mathrm{et}}))$ for every integer $a$. It sends every bounded-below normalized system to a bounded-below normalized system, with normalization as explicitly defined in [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. These assertions are for actual functors and natural transformations in the derived category of strict coefficient systems, including their map action and independence of complex resolutions.

For a finite extension $E\subset E'$ with $O'=\mathcal O_{E'}$, use the coefficient system $B_n=O'/\varpi^nO'$ and the exact levelwise extension of scalars $T_{B/A}$ (each $B_n$ is finite free over $A_n$). The canonical scalar comparison is an isomorphism of functors of derived systems
$$T_{B/A}G_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f,B}T_{B/A}.$$
Here $G_{f,B}$ is the same right-adjoint construction with $O'$ and the non-zero-divisor $\varpi$; normalization is relative to its powers. These comparisons respect the identity extension and composition, quotient maps and the canonical tensor associators. If $\varpi'$ is a uniformizer of $O'$ and $e$ is the ramification index, $\varpi^nO'=(\varpi')^{en}O'$, so restriction to these levels is the cofinal subsequence of the system indexed by powers of $\varpi'$. Restricting the construction to that subsequence agrees with the construction just stated, including its maps. No inverse limit, completed integral output, constructible restriction or pro-etale exceptional adjoint is asserted in this lemma.

source.place: Constructions 5.14–5.15, Lemma 5.16 and the Brown adjoint following it (printed pp. 34–35); Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.24 (printed pp. 36–37), with the bounded-below equivalence of normalization conditions in Lemma 4.13 (printed p. 24). The finite-free scalar comparison is the finite-free instance of the tensor/adjunction construction in Proposition 2.29(2) and its system version in Construction 5.15; cofinal indexing uses Construction 4.1. The bound c_f follows from the finite cohomological amplitude [0,2d] in Construction 5.15 by adjunction.

proof.text: Apply the Brown construction to $O$ and $t=\varpi$. It supplies the actual $O$-linear exact system functor $F=Rp_{A,*}j_{!,A}$, its coproduct-preserving property and exact right adjoint $G$. The coefficient projection maps give the canonical left-extension comparisons $FL_n\cong L_nF_n$, including transitions.

Apply the evaluation-and-bound lemma to this adjunction and its specified left-extension comparisons. It gives $e_nG\cong f_n^\times e_n$ with evaluated units, counits and transition mates. The finite-level amplitude theorem supplies $N_f$, independent of $n$; the same lemma gives $G(D^{\ge a})\subset D^{\ge a-N_f}$. Set $c_f=N_f$. In Lean the recorded Brown realization is identified with the exact constant-scalar restriction localized to derived categories. Its ordinary functor is faithful and exact, so it preserves and reflects the standard upper cohomological bound. The realization comparison then transfers the finite-coefficient amplitude to the strict level compact-support functor.

The nonflat coefficient-mate lemma makes each $b_{m,n}$ invertible. For a normalized $M$, its output transition is $g_n(t^M_{m,n})b_{m,n}$ by step 2, hence is invertible. Thus $GM$ is normalized; the lower bound in step 2 also makes it bounded below when $M$ is bounded below. For the invertible quotientComparison field of the strict record, the Brown projection normalization is the inverse-image face of an exchange-mate cube. The two vertical realization mates are invertible because the realization functors are equivalences. The cube therefore transfers invertibility of the finite-coefficient quotient mate to the strict quotient mate.

For $E\subset E'$, the local-field coefficient-stage theorem gives finite free $B_n/A_n$ and $\varpi^nO'=(\varpi')^{en}O'$ with $e\ge1$. In particular levelwise extension $T_{B/A}$ is exact, and the positive indices $en$ are cofinal. Apply steps 1 and 2 also to $O'$, once with its nonzero nonunit $\varpi$ (giving $G_{f,B}$ with its evaluated adjunction and transition-mate identifications) and once with $\varpi'$ (the full tower used in step 6).

Apply the scalar-mate coherence lemma to these two adjunctions. Its counit-transpose map gives $T_{B/A}G_A\cong G_BT_{B/A}$ as an actual derived-system transformation. Its identity, composition and mixed quotient equations are precisely the requested coherences under canonical tensor associators. The identity assertion is proved directly in Lean: tensor-unit normalization determines the levelwise identity, faithful forgetting proves successor compatibility, and localization descends the ordinary identity to the derived category with the specified representative formula. Tensor-unit normalization similarly identifies the inverse-image squares; adjunction transposition identifies the open and proper squares and therefore the compact-support square. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom equivalence proves the exceptional identity. No faithfulness of derived evaluation is used in this argument. For composition, the Lean proof uses lem-pur-strict-etale-compact-support-composition on the three compact-support transport records. Applying injectivity of the third adjunction Hom equivalence, its counit formula twice and naturality proves the exceptional cocycle from the inverse projection cocycle. No exceptional adjoint is included in the new geometric premise. The coefficient changes, exact transports, inverse-image, compact-support and composition records used by these statements are those of [def-pur-strict-etale-coefficient-transport-interfaces].

For cofinal transport derive e≥1 and the equality of principal powers from the local-field coefficient-stage theorem, identifying its integer-ring map with strictEtaleIntegerMap on field representatives. Prove r(n)+1=e(n+1), including n=0. The quotient equivalences define bijective stage maps. Invoke the strictly geometric isomorphic-stage projection bridge to obtain exact coefficient transports and the left-adjoint evaluation and quotient cubes. Finite-level scalar functors are equivalences, so the finite exceptional mates are invertible. Define the actual system comparison as the mate of inverse compact-support projection. Applying exchangeMate_cube to the evaluation cube proves its evaluation equation. Evaluation jointly detects isomorphisms, so this mate is invertible. Apply exchangeMate_cube again to the quotient cube; substitute the two exceptional quotient-mate normalizations and expand the symmetric quotient tensor interchanges to obtain the mixed quotient equation. Assemble the unchanged strict exceptional transport record. The arithmetic and both mate-cube calculations are complete Lean proofs; only geometric projection realization is split off.

Scalar transport remains unchanged.
